# Ephe engine advisory register — flaws that reach us through a native engine
#
# This file exists because the Python register cannot see this class of flaw at all.
# `pip-audit` asks the PyPI ecosystem about the *pip package*; the cell's execution
# engine is Rust, shipped inside the `wasmtime` wheel as a compiled library, and its
# advisories live in the crates.io/RustSec ecosystem. Measured 2026-10-09:
# `POST https://api.osv.dev/v1/query` for `{package: wasmtime, ecosystem: PyPI,
# version: 47.0.1}` returns **zero** vulnerabilities, while the same engine version in
# the `wasmtime-wasi` crate range is under an active advisory. So an entry here is
# never a `--ignore-vuln` flag — pip-audit would not have reported it.
# `.github/workflows/supply-chain.yml` resolves every ID in this file and in
# `advisories-ignore.txt` against the advisory databases, failing the run on an ID
# that resolves nowhere (that is how `GHSA-j2g9-4prp-pf6h` was nearly lost: a
# well-formed ID that only exists as an *alias*, which the naive lookup reads as a 404).
#
# Line format: <ID>  # package=<name> ecosystem=<eco> probe=<version>
#                    affected=<range> fixed_in=<version> state=fixed
#                    alias=<the GHSA string for the same record, if any> recheck=<YYYY-MM-DD>
# `probe` is the version the resolution check asks the databases about. An entry
# without `state=fixed` is a written acceptance and must also name `blocked_by`, the
# constraint that keeps the fix out of reach, plus the exposure that was measured and
# what remains UNPROVEN. Past its recheck date the gate fails, same rule as the other
# register: the decision carries the date it stops being valid.
#
# 2026-10-23, owner decision D29: the engine moved from 48.0.0 to 50.0.1.
# Why that version: RUSTSEC-2026-0352 (GHSA-m9f7-9w4p-gv38) is a filesystem sandbox
# escape when renaming symlinks with trailing slashes, and PyPI publishes no fixed
# 48.x (48.0.6) and no fixed 49.0.3. 50.0.1 is the first published release outside
# every affected range below. Ephemora Cell 1.1.0 declares `wasmtime<48`; the uv
# override in pyproject.toml replaces that bound, and `tests/test_cell_runtime_floor.py`
# holds both the floor and the lock to it.
# Evidence for the move: 142 cell, sandbox and fence tests passed on 50.0.1 on
# 2026-10-23 (out/s4-20261023-_5_914gn/cell-tests-wasmtime50.log), including the cell
# boot, the policy snapshot and the WASIConfig seam. The four cap figures in
# core/cpython_cell.py were measured on the 47.x engine; re-running one live cell on
# 50.0.1 is the next measurement, and until it runs this register does not claim the
# fuel-per-second figure is re-measured.

# GHSA-j2g9-4prp-pf6h = RUSTSEC-2026-0314 (the RustSec entry is the primary record;
# the GHSA string is an alias of it, and the canonical advisory sits in the
# bytecodealliance/wasmtime repository, not in the pip ecosystem).
RUSTSEC-2026-0314  # package=wasmtime-wasi ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=37.0.0,<48.0.3 fixed_in=48.0.3 state=fixed alias=GHSA-j2g9-4prp-pf6h recheck=2027-01-23

RUSTSEC-2026-0321  # package=wasmtime-wasi ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=37.0.0,<48.0.4 fixed_in=48.0.4 state=fixed alias=GHSA-j366-h8gg-77pm recheck=2027-01-23

RUSTSEC-2026-0322  # package=wasmtime-wasi ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=37.0.0,<48.0.4 fixed_in=48.0.4 state=fixed alias=GHSA-gqmc-89g8-p25r recheck=2027-01-23

RUSTSEC-2026-0323  # package=wasmtime-wasi ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=37.0.0,<48.0.4 fixed_in=48.0.4 state=fixed alias=GHSA-96f6-r43r-8c24 recheck=2027-01-23

RUSTSEC-2026-0324  # package=wasmtime-wasi ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=48.0.0,<48.0.4 fixed_in=48.0.4 state=fixed alias=GHSA-mr2v-56j5-cmfc recheck=2027-01-23

# Filesystem sandbox escape when renaming symlinks with trailing slashes.
# CVSS v4 AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:L/SC:H/SI:H/SA:L.
# Fixed ranges: 36.0.18, 48.0.6 and 49.0.3 — none of the latter two are on PyPI.
RUSTSEC-2026-0352  # package=wasmtime-wasi ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=37.0.0,<48.0.6 fixed_in=48.0.6 state=fixed alias=GHSA-m9f7-9w4p-gv38 recheck=2027-01-23

# 2026-11-03 — what was missing here was a probe target.
# Every row above names the `wasmtime-wasi` crate, and `--audit-engine` asks the
# database only about the (package, ecosystem, probe) triples written here. The
# engine that executes guest code is the `wasmtime` crate itself, and no line ever
# named it — so an advisory against `wasmtime` could reach this register as nothing.
# Measured the same day: `{package: wasmtime, ecosystem: crates.io, version: 50.0.1}`
# returns zero records. That is a verdict, and the register had never asked the
# question. This row asks it. It claims no live exposure.
# RUSTSEC-2026-0379 (aliases CVE-2026-115893, GHSA-mghf-wjfp-p5xm): the Cranelift
# backend on aarch64 can jump to an incorrect target on a large Wasm `br_table`, so a
# valid module escapes the guest. OSV events, copied out of the record:
# introduced 0.0.0-0 fixed 36.0.19; introduced 37.0.0 fixed 48.0.7; introduced 49.0.0
# fixed 49.0.4. 50.0.1 is outside all three. x86-64 was not affected; this Mac is.
RUSTSEC-2026-0379  # package=wasmtime ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=49.0.0,<49.0.4 fixed_in=49.0.4 state=fixed alias=GHSA-mghf-wjfp-p5xm recheck=2027-02-03

# 2026-11-23 — the nine records that reach the locked engine, measured against the
# database and against this product. OSV reports, for {wasmtime, crates.io, 50.0.1},
# eight records (RUSTSEC-2026-0566..0573), and for {wasmtime-wasi, crates.io, 50.0.1},
# one more (RUSTSEC-2026-0587). All nine publish a fix on crates.io — 50.0.2 for the
# wasmtime eight, 50.0.3 for the wasi one — and PyPI publishes neither of those wheel
# versions: measured against pypi.org/pypi/wasmtime/json the 50.x line carries only
# 50.0.1; 51.0.0 is the next release, and the databases report ZERO records for
# wasmtime@51.0.0 and wasmtime-wasi@51.0.0 (queried 2026-11-23, full run in
# /Users/sanji/ephe-plan/osv-wasmtime/). A crate with a published fix is moved, not
# talked out of it: every row below is a written acceptance whose blocked_by names
# exactly that open move, and the move is to the 51.0.0 wheel, not to the wheel versions
# that were never published. These rows carry no state=fixed until 51.0.0 is locked.
#
# What the cell actually runs, measured 2026-11-23. ONE vendor builder sets every
# engine flag (the ephemora_cell 1.1.0 wheel, `_engine_config.py:46-68`; the only
# in-tree call site is tests/test_cell_runtime_floor.py:98): wasm_threads,
# wasm_multi_memory, wasm_function_references, wasm_exceptions, wasm_gc, wasm_tail_call
# and wasm_stack_switching are set False there. memory64 is a per-config opt-in the
# product never passes (core/cpython_cell.py:221-230 and core/tools/sandbox_tools.py:66-73
# build WASIConfig without it; the wheel default is False at wasi_runtime.py:302), so it
# is off at both seams. SIMD is never touched by the builder and stays compiled and on —
# no row below depends on it either way. The product cell runs preview1
# (core/cpython_cell.py:231), no sockets and no fork (core/cpython_cell.py:26); the
# wheel fails an unknown non-WASI import at instantiate (wasi_runtime.py:315), the
# component world does not link wasi:http at all (wasi_02.py:25) and links wasi:sockets
# with connect denied at call time (wasi_02.py:27; egress_sidecar.py:6 — "The guest has
# NO sockets"). The component path IS reachable through the opt-in sandbox tool, which
# takes a host path with abi="auto" (core/tools/sandbox_tools.py:74) — that is the door
# the stream and component rows (0566, 0572) are written against, not the CPython cell.
#
# UNPROVEN, so the rows do not claim more than they measured: the cargo feature set the
# wheel was compiled with is not readable from the Python half, so the two
# "builds-without-the-feature" aborts (0567, 0570) are written OFF by config, not
# proven off by build; whether any host function calls Caller::get_module_export
# outside a guest call (0569) sits inside the compiled engine; and 0587 is a Windows
# path — install.ps1 is a first-class surface (AGENTS.md) and PyPI ships win_amd64 and
# win_arm64 wheels for 50.0.1 AND 51.0.0 (measured 2026-11-23), so the premise stands,
# but no Windows host was run here.

# wasmtime-wasi unbounded host memory growth via empty writes to wasi:io AsyncWriteStream.
# Exposure as measured: component streams only — the CPython cell is preview1 with sync
# fd_write (core/cpython_cell.py:231), and the one component door is the sandbox tool's
# abi=auto on a caller-named path (core/tools/sandbox_tools.py:74).
# UNPROVEN: an attacker plant of a component module through that path.
RUSTSEC-2026-0566  # package=wasmtime ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=50.0.0,<50.0.2 fixed_in=50.0.2 state=accepted blocked_by=pypi-publishes-neither-50.0.2-50.0.3-wheel-and-override-pins-lt51 recheck=2026-12-23

# Abort in wasmtime builds compiled without the threads cargo feature.
# Exposure as measured: wasm_threads is set False in the vendor's single builder
# (ephemora_cell/_engine_config.py:53), so no guest enables threads.
# UNPROVEN: the cargo feature set the wheel itself was compiled with.
RUSTSEC-2026-0567  # package=wasmtime ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=50.0.0,<50.0.2 fixed_in=50.0.2 state=accepted blocked_by=pypi-publishes-neither-50.0.2-50.0.3-wheel-and-override-pins-lt51 recheck=2026-12-23

# Stale GC heap base pointer (CVSS AV:L/AC:H/PR:L A:H).
# Exposure as measured: wasm_gc is set False (ephemora_cell/_engine_config.py:62), so
# guest code never reaches GC-compiled paths; validation rejects GC instructions.
# UNPROVEN: nothing further beyond the compile-time question shared with 0570.
RUSTSEC-2026-0568  # package=wasmtime ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=50.0.0,<50.0.2 fixed_in=50.0.2 state=accepted blocked_by=pypi-publishes-neither-50.0.2-50.0.3-wheel-and-override-pins-lt51 recheck=2026-12-23

# Panic in Caller::get_module_export when a host function is not called from Wasm.
# Exposure as measured: no call site in product code — core/ drives the engine only
# through run_isolated (core/cpython_cell.py:231, core/tools/sandbox_tools.py:74).
# UNPROVEN: host-function internals inside the compiled wheel.
RUSTSEC-2026-0569  # package=wasmtime ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=50.0.0,<50.0.2 fixed_in=50.0.2 state=accepted blocked_by=pypi-publishes-neither-50.0.2-50.0.3-wheel-and-override-pins-lt51 recheck=2026-12-23

# Abort in wasmtime builds compiled without the gc cargo feature.
# Exposure as measured: wasm_gc is set False (ephemora_cell/_engine_config.py:62);
# guests cannot turn GC on from their side.
# UNPROVEN: the cargo feature set the wheel itself was compiled with.
RUSTSEC-2026-0570  # package=wasmtime ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=50.0.0,<50.0.2 fixed_in=50.0.2 state=accepted blocked_by=pypi-publishes-neither-50.0.2-50.0.3-wheel-and-override-pins-lt51 recheck=2026-12-23

# wasmtime-wasi-http unbounded heap via empty body writes on HTTP/2.
# Exposure as measured: wasi:http is never linked into the guest (wasi_02.py:25 —
# unknown imports fail at instantiate, wasi_runtime.py:315) and the cell has no
# network at all (core/cpython_cell.py:26, egress_sidecar.py:6).
# UNPROVEN: none — no path reaches an HTTP/2 stream from the product.
RUSTSEC-2026-0571  # package=wasmtime ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=50.0.0,<50.0.2 fixed_in=50.0.2 state=accepted blocked_by=pypi-publishes-neither-50.0.2-50.0.3-wheel-and-override-pins-lt51 recheck=2026-12-23

# Panic when a component cancels a stream/future copy on the wrong end.
# Exposure as measured: component path only; the CPython cell is preview1
# (core/cpython_cell.py:231) and the component door is the sandbox tool's abi=auto
# (core/tools/sandbox_tools.py:74), which takes a caller-named host path.
# UNPROVEN: an attacker plant of a crafted component through that tool.
RUSTSEC-2026-0572  # package=wasmtime ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=50.0.0,<50.0.2 fixed_in=50.0.2 state=accepted blocked_by=pypi-publishes-neither-50.0.2-50.0.3-wheel-and-override-pins-lt51 recheck=2026-12-23

# Process abort when the GC heap reservation is not a multiple of the page size.
# Exposure as measured: wasm_gc is set False (ephemora_cell/_engine_config.py:62),
# so no GC heap reservation is ever made for guest code.
# UNPROVEN: nothing further beyond the compile-time question shared with 0570.
RUSTSEC-2026-0573  # package=wasmtime ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=50.0.0,<50.0.2 fixed_in=50.0.2 state=accepted blocked_by=pypi-publishes-neither-50.0.2-50.0.3-wheel-and-override-pins-lt51 recheck=2026-12-23

# wasmtime-wasi filesystem sandbox escape on Windows via a drive-prefixed path
# component (CVSS 4.0 AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:P VC:H/VI:H/VA:H).
# Exposure as measured: the cell ships to Windows — install.ps1 is a first-class
# product surface (AGENTS.md) and PyPI publishes win_amd64/win_arm64 wasmtime
# wheels for 50.0.1 and 51.0.0 alike (measured 2026-11-23).
# UNPROVEN: no Windows host was run here; the escape itself was not reproduced.
RUSTSEC-2026-0587  # package=wasmtime-wasi ecosystem=crates.io probe=50.0.1 affected=>=50.0.0,<50.0.3 fixed_in=50.0.3 state=accepted blocked_by=pypi-publishes-neither-50.0.2-50.0.3-wheel-and-override-pins-lt51 recheck=2026-12-23
